sub_agendas_items.title: Engineer’s Report for the McKinnons Creek Municipal Drain

attachments.attachment_title: 4.1 - ACS2025-IWS-WL-0014 - Doc 3 - McKinnons Creek MD - Bylaw.pdf

sub_agendas_items.description:
File No. ACS2025-IWS-WL-0014 - Orléans South-Navan (19)
Deferred from the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee Meeting of September 4, 2025.
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the outset, the Committee received a detailed slide presentation from Mr. Lorne Franklin, Robinson Consultants Inc., which served as an overview of the Municipal Drainage works for the McKinnons Creek Municipal Drain. A copy of this presentation is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
Mr. Andy Robinson, P.Eng., Robinson Consultants Inc., and Mr. Dave Ryan, Drainage Superintendent, Infrastructure and Water Service Department were also present to respond to questions.
Correspondence was received from Mr. Andre Grzela and from Mr. Wendell Watson. Both submissions are held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.Following questions to staff and discussions, the report recommendations were put before Committee and were ‘Carried’, as presented, with Councillor C. Kitts dissenting.

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend that Council adopt the engineer’s report prepared by Robinson Consultants Inc., entitled Engineer’s report for the McKinnons Creek Municipal Drain, and give first and second readings to the By-law attached as Document 3 in accordance with Sections 42 and 45 of theDrainage Act of Ontario.

sub_agendas_items.title: Independent Electricity Service Operator (IESO) Long Term 2 (LT2) Procurement – Requests for Municipal Support Confirmation in the Rural Area

attachments.attachment_title: 6.1 - ACS2025-SI-CCR-0010 - Doc 13 - Municipal Support Confirmation Template Form.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the outset, Vice-Chair C. Kelly read out the following amending Motion:
The Committee then received the following public delegations:
[ *    Individuals / groups marked with an asterisk above provided slide presentations to accompany their verbal addresses to Committee; all presentations are held on file with the Office of the City Clerk. ]
Following questions to the delegations, Vice-Chair C. Kelly moved the following:
Motion No. ARAC 2025-28-02
Moved by Vice-Chair C. Kelly:
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa has previously entered into host municipality responsibility agreements with third-party project proponents who provide funds related to community initiatives in recognition of the project’s effects on the local community; and
WHEREAS host municipality responsibility agreements generally provide for the City to determine how to allocate and disburse funds provided by the third party in order to respond to community needs and ensure accountability and transparency, with eligible community initiatives often identified by City staff in consultation with the relevant Ward Councillor(s);
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff, in the event these projects proceed, be directed to request that the proposed Dunrobin Solar Project and Carp Airport Solar Project proponents be encouraged to enter into a host municipality responsibility agreement with the City of Ottawa, consistent with other host municipality responsibility agreements previously entered into by the City,  through which the proponent would provide an amount of at least $1000 per megawatt per year with the goal to achieve a higher amount if possible, for a period of not less than 20 years. The finalization and execution of such agreement shall be approved by Council, with recommendations to be provided as to the allocation and disbursements of such funds;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff be directed to provide City Council with an update on the status of the request to the proponents by way of memorandum within three months following the issuance of a contract by the Independent Electricity Systems Operator (IESO) for the Dunrobin Solar Project and Carp Airport Solar Project, and to bring forward for committee and Council approval any draft host municipality responsibility agreements negotiated with the proponents.
Ms Nichole Hoover-Bienasz, Director, Climate Change and Resiliency, Strategic Initiatives Department, was present to respond to questions.  Following questions to staff and at the conclusion of discussions, the Committee considered the Motions as follows:
Motion No. ARAC 2025-28-01
Moved by Vice-Chair C. Kelly:
WHEREAS Report ACS2025-SI-CCR-0010 was issued with the agenda on September 22, 2025; and
WHEREAS staff were informed by Portage Power, the proponent of three projects proposed within Ward 21 (Rideau-Jock), that the requests for the granting of Municipal Support Confirmation for the proposed solar energy generation projects know as Richmond Solar I, Richmond Solar II and Richmond Solar III are withdrawn at this time;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee approve the withdrawal of Recommendations 1, 2 and 3 of report ACS2025-Si-CCR-0010 at the request of the proponent.
Carried
Motion No. ARAC 2025-28-02
Moved by Vice-Chair C. Kelly:
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa has previously entered into host municipality responsibility agreements with third-party project proponents who provide funds related to community initiatives in recognition of the project’s effects on the local community; and
WHEREAS host municipality responsibility agreements generally provide for the City to determine how to allocate and disburse funds provided by the third party in order to respond to community needs and ensure accountability and transparency, with eligible community initiatives often identified by City staff in consultation with the relevant Ward Councillor(s);
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff, in the event these projects proceed, be directed to request that the proposed Dunrobin Solar Project and Carp Airport Solar Project proponents be encouraged to enter into a host municipality responsibility agreement with the City of Ottawa, consistent with other host municipality responsibility agreements previously entered into by the City,  through which the proponent would provide an amount of at least $1000 per megawatt per year with the goal to achieve a higher amount if possible, for a period of not less than 20 years. The finalization and execution of such agreement shall be approved by Council, with recommendations to be provided as to the allocation and disbursements of such funds;
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff be directed to provide City Council with an update on the status of the request to the proponents by way of memorandum within three months following the issuance of a contract by the Independent Electricity Systems Operator (IESO) for the Dunrobin Solar Project and Carp Airport Solar Project, and to bring forward for committee and Council approval any draft host municipality responsibility agreements negotiated with the proponents.
Carried
The Committee then considered the report recommendations, as amended (Chair D. Brown noted that when such procurement applications and Municipal Support Confirmation requests come forward, Committee had asked that each project be considered individually; hence, each of the functional clauses of the report recommendations, as amended, were voted upon separately):
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend that Council grant a Municipal Support Confirmation (MSC), for the purposes of satisfying the mandatory requirements under Section 4.2(c) of the LT2(e-1) RFP, which does not supersede any applicable permits or approvals under applicable Laws and Regulations that may be required for a Long-Term Energy Project, to: 
Carried as amended
The report recommendations were then put before Committee and were ‘Carried’, as amended by Motions No. ARAC 2025-28-01 and ARAC 2025-28-02.
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend Council:
Carried as amended
